title: feat(sim): carry machined stock into a setup turned side-on
body:
## What changed

A setup that stands the part on its edge can now take "What Setup1 leaves behind" as its stock. The turn is a quarter turn about X or Y from the setup before it. Before this change the carry was refused by name (`CARRY_TURN_REFUSAL`).

**camcraft-sim** (`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/carry_side.rs`, new):

- `SideTurn` is one of the sixteen side-on quarter turns. `CarryTurn` is a lattice turn or a side turn.
- `Body::carry_side` reads the column body again along the new tool axis:
  - The level axis that stays level is re-indexed, centre onto centre.
  - The old heights become slabs of one cell, centred on the old Z range. A face inside a slab counts the slab whole.
  - The old level axis becomes the height. The top and the floor are the hull of the old column centres that hold material. Each end moves out to the next centre that holds no material, or to the lattice edge. A cavity between the ends is filled.
- The carried body is never smaller than the body the columns hold. It is at most one grid cell larger on a turned face. The raw faces of a box stock at the lattice edge are read exactly.
- The field engine refuses a side-on turn by name (`FIELD_SIDE_CARRY_REFUSAL`). The shipped engine is the column engine.
- `CARRY_TURN_REFUSAL` has shorter words: "the stock simulation carries machined stock only through quarter turns (steps of 90° about X, Y or Z)". A turn off the quarter is still refused and the app still names the turn and the two setups.

**camcraft-app**:

- `stock_sim_carry.rs`: `carry_turn` returns a `CarryTurn`. The program walk judges the body before a side-on turn and keeps those gouges for the final verdict. The hull can hide a gouge that an earlier setup cut. This is the same fold that a block left for a new block gets (#320).
- `side_on_note` adds a note line to the gate: the stock was turned side-on, and what the verdict reads.
- `rest/across.rs` and `rest.rs` hold a `CarryTurn`. The rest reading, the judged stock, the prior plan and the carried block follow the same turn. The `Debug` text of a lattice turn is unchanged, so no shipped stamp moves.

No user-facing command is new. No MCP tool is owed.

## How it was tested

Pinning tests:

- `crates/app/tests/setup_carry_side.rs`
  - `a_faced_plate_carries_side_on_with_its_volume_and_verdict` (the "Done means" test: volume, size, clean verdict, and a 1 mm gouge in Setup2 is found)
  - `a_gouge_cut_before_a_side_on_turn_still_reads_in_the_verdict`
  - `the_verdict_says_the_stock_was_turned_side_on`
  - `the_field_engine_refuses_the_side_on_carry_by_name`
- `crates/sim/tests/stock_carry_side.rs` (14 tests: exact block, steps on both sides, reversed axes, a filled cavity, a face inside a slab, a thin plate, there and back, the verdict, each refusal, the digest text)
- `crates/app/tests/setup_stock_source.rs`: `a_side_on_turn_between_setups_carries_and_a_skew_turn_is_refused_naming_the_turn` replaces the #866 test that pinned the side-on refusal. The test count of the file is the same.

Mutation checks. Each line was removed or changed, the named test went red, the file was restored, and `cmp` against the backup was identical:

| Line | Test that went red |
|---|---|
| non-finite refusal (`SideTurn::from_matrix`) | `turns_off_the_quarter_are_refused_by_name` |
| off-quarter entry refusal | same |
| not-a-permutation refusal | same |
| mirror refusal | same |
| not-side-on refusal | same |
| field-engine refusal | `the_field_engine_refuses_a_side_on_turn_by_name` |
| too-tall refusal | `a_body_too_tall_for_the_turned_lattice_is_refused_by_name` |
| high-side pad (never short) | `a_step_turned_side_on_is_never_read_short` |
| low-side pad (never short) | `a_step_on_the_low_side_is_never_read_short_either` |
| floor flag dropped after the turn | `a_clean_block_turned_side_on_reads_no_gouge_and_no_judged_floor` |
| slab counted whole | `a_face_inside_a_slab_counts_the_slab_whole` |
| gouge kept before a side-on turn | `a_gouge_cut_before_a_side_on_turn_still_reads_in_the_verdict` |
| side-on note on the gate | `the_verdict_says_the_stock_was_turned_side_on` |
| note only for a side-on carry | same |
| lattice-turn digest text | `the_two_kinds_of_turn_are_told_apart` |

Gate. `cargo xtask gate quick --dry-run` selected about 180 app suites, because the gate map of many suites names `sim::stock_sim`. The run was therefore done by name:

- sim: every suite of the quick plan (the lib and 32 test binaries), all green.
- app: the lib (313 tests) and `setup_carry_side`, `setup_stock_source`, `setup_carry`, `carried_verify`, `rest_across_setups`, `carried_engine_agreement`, `carried_fixtures_cache`, `carried_corner_rest`, `between_setups`, `setups`, `setup_align`, `stock_sim_document`, `post_not_judged`, `stock_engine_agreement`, `stock_view`, `fixtures`, `probe_only_sim`, all green.
- ui: `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib setup_stock` (4 tests), green.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`, clean.

## What was not exercised

- The batch tier and the other app suites of the quick plan.
- The pixel snapshots. No snapshot PNG changed.
- Windows and macOS. The run was on Linux.
- The prior plan on a job thread (`PriorPlan::simulate`) with a side-on turn. Its change is one call (`carry_through`).
- A carried fixture at a turned face. See the known limits.

## Known limits

- A wall that the tool flank cut, or a step, is read up to one cell outside the real face after the turn. The verdict can show rest of up to one cell on a finished face. The carried-fixture law (#321) can refuse a fixture that touches such a face. The workaround is the setup's own stock. The follow-up issue for the exact carry is linked in the issue comments.
- A cavity seen from the side is filled. Rest machining in the turned setup can cut air there. It never meets uncut material.
- The verdict taken before the turn does not credit the edge breaks and marks of the earlier setup. The fold for a new block (#320) has the same limit.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/874-side-on-carry.md`. Branch from upstream `main` at 6c33940d.

Changelog: A setup turned side-on (a quarter turn about X or Y) can take the machined stock of the setup before it; the carried stock is never smaller than the real stock, and a gouge cut before the turn stays in the verdict.

Effort: max (not escalated)

The status strip gains a Report door next to the Debug info door (#1696).

- The numbers with no public source are left out: guide heights, AWT, wire diameters, conditions and codes. The app refuses a cut by name until the user adds a condition from their own control.

Rework after the review:
- Taper source: the figure of 25 degrees stays. The Sodick Thailand page https://www.sodick.co.th/EN/EDW.php lists the ALC400G taper angle as +-25 deg at work height 130 mm. - Taper limit: the taper figure is data only. The file states no guide heights, so the post refuses a tapered cut by name. The post also finds no wire plane in the machine file, so it would refuse the cut for that reason too. The schema gap is tracked in #1800. This PR changes no schema, no post code and no posted G-code.
- The machine file now carries a `general.description` with the sources and this limit.

- https://www.sodick.co.th/EN/EDW.php (taper, travels)

title: fix(edm): count orbit radius in sinker rough and finish sizing

## What changed

Sinker rough and finish passes accept an orbit.
The size law counts electrode width plus twice the spark gap and orbit radius.
The tip stands undersize minus orbit radius above the finished floor.
Overburns refuse by name.
A finish vector pattern must reach all four walls, so its direction count must be a multiple of four.

## Cause

The size law counted spark gap alone.
The interim command guard refused every rough or finish orbit to prevent an unsafe judgment.

## Tests

The app pins failed on unchanged production code before the fix.

- `orbited_rough_finish_pair_reaches_size_in_sim` checks circular, four-direction vector, and planetary passes. Each finish has a clean verdict, zero gouge, and rest within simulation resolution.
- `orbit_that_would_overburn_the_cavity_is_refused_by_name` checks rough and finish refusals.
- `finish_orbit_without_full_axis_reach_is_refused_by_name` checks incomplete vector patterns.
- `sinker_undersize_counts_orbit_width_and_keeps_the_floor` checks the shared size and floor law.
- `sinker_undersize_checks_orbit_before_judging_it` checks malformed orbit inputs.

Copying all three production files from upstream/main made the app pins fail again.
Restoring the fix made them pass.
Four individual mutations also failed their pins and passed after restoration: omit radius from width, restore the old floor stand, disable partial-vector refusal, and omit orbit validation.

The motion undersize unit tests passed 3 tests.

title: feat(sinker): compensate a Sinker Side Burn for electrode wear in Z
body:
## What changed

- `camcraft-motion`: new `sinker_side::side_burn_worn`. The plunge is the layered, wear-compensated plunge of `sinker_wear::burn_compensated`, with all of its refusals (rate, layer step, electrode length, deepest-tip bound). The lateral move and its return run at the last compensated tip. The tip is checked against the deepest-tip bound. With no wear and no layer step, the moves and notes are the same as `side_burn`.
- `camcraft-app`: `SinkerSideBurnOp::refusal` no longer refuses a sound measured wear or layer step. The constants `SIDE_WEAR_REFUSAL` and `SIDE_LAYER_REFUSAL` are removed. A half-stated wear or a bad layer step is still refused by name (#546's refusals). `generate_sinker_side` calls `side_burn_worn` with `sinker_wear_op::side_wear` (the measured wear and the layer step only). `sinker_wear_op::judged` reads the side burn's moves as the worn electrode burns them, so the stock sim judges the real cavity.
- `camcraft-ui`: the side burn page shows the Layer step, Measured wear and Measured over rows, with a wear status line (`side_wear_status`).
- Decision: `docs/decisions/1340-side-burn-wear.md`. Only the measured wear applies to a side burn. The condition's `wear` rate is not applied, so a saved side burn posts byte for byte. Side wear is not compensated: a worn electrode is smaller, so the wall is left short, never cut past the allowance.

The MCP params door already carries `wear_lost`, `wear_over` and `layer` for a side burn: `SinkerSideDto` flattens the burn DTO (`project/sinker_dto.rs`). No new MCP tool is necessary.

## How tested

- `camcraft-motion` unit tests: `sinker_side_worn_off_is_the_plain_side_burn`, `sinker_side_worn_plunges_in_compensated_layers_and_moves_at_the_deepest_tip`, `sinker_side_worn_keeps_every_refusal_by_name`.
- `crates/app/tests/sinker_side.rs`: `a_worn_side_burn_is_compensated_in_z_and_judged_clean` (replaces `a_side_burn_with_a_wear_rate_is_refused_by_name`). It checks the layer tips, the lateral move at the deepest tip, no move below that tip, a stock sim with no gouge, create/edit/paste/file doors, and that a condition's wear does not change a plain side burn.
- The golden `sinker_side_burn.cl` is unchanged. `sinker_wear` suite is green.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: green.

## Not exercised

- No real EDM control. The fixtures are synthetic.
- The UI rows were not opened in the GUI. No structural UI test was added for them.
- Pixel snapshots (release lane).

title: fix(post): refuse unsupported Sodick angle-word moves
body:
## What changed

Keep Sodick constant taper refused until its mapping preserves the generated wire path.
Refuse WireAngle records by operation name even when the section omits WireTaper.
Stop cutting that section instead of silently writing a vertical move.
Record the evidence and rejected mappings in docs/decisions/1496-sodick-taper.md.
This uses the issue's allowed outcome of documenting the mapping limits and retaining refusal.

## Cause

The post ignored WireAngle records.
A direct angle-word stream without WireTaper could therefore emit a vertical cut without a warning.
Lower-guide XY and explicit upper-guide offsets cannot simply become nominal A angles without proving the corner and transition motion.
The alternative angle stream uses work-relative WirePlane, which does not establish Sodick's table-relative program height.

Sodick's [2012 LN1W/LN2W training manual](https://fab.cba.mit.edu/content/tools/sodick_edm/sodick_user_manual_small.pdf), printed pages 66-70, describes G51/G52, A, G50 and the table/guide settings.
That newer-control source does not prove the complete mapping for this post's Mark 21/EX21 target.
Unconfirmed items are Mark 21/EX21 TP/TN initialization and datum/calibration correspondence, corner and lead/cancel interpolation, and the signed angle mapping in that frame.
No unconfirmed words are emitted.

## Tests

`sodick_refuses_angle_words_even_without_section_taper` fails on the original post and passes with the guard.
It covers positive, negative and zero angles.
`sodick_vertical_stream_still_posts_without_angle_words` preserves vertical posting.
Mutation: restoring assets/posts/sodick-wire.cps from upstream/main makes the refusal pin fail again.
Restoring the fix makes both pins pass.
`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passes the selected post and app suites.
`cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes.

None.

No physical Sodick control was exercised.
No tapered output or tapered golden is added.
The targeted Mark 21/EX21 mapping remains unverified.

title: fix(2d): cut an open Contour run on its air side
body:
## What changed

A Contour on an open run of a part (an edge chain that does not close) no longer moves the tool centre along the run. The tool centre now stands one tool radius plus the stock to leave off the run, on the side that has no part material.

- New `machining2d::contour_open_run` in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_run_side.rs`.
  - It reads the part section at each cut level, 0.01 mm above the level.
  - It tests two points 0.05 mm left and right of each run segment to find the side with material.
  - It offsets the run to the other side (the air side) and cuts it with `contour_along_chain`.
  - Climb keeps the material on the right of the tool (#1555). Conventional goes the other way.
- It refuses the run by name in these conditions:
  - The run has part material on both sides at a level.
  - The material side changes between levels or along the run.
  - The tool beside the run overlaps the part (for example, the run ends at a wall).
  - The offset folds onto itself.
- A run with no part material beside it at any level keeps the old centreline ride. The path note tells this.
- `generate.rs` (Contour, selection arm) calls the new function when the picks are on a finished part (`part_solid`). Picks on the stock keep the old ride. The run's notes now go into the path (the `stitch` helper drops them).
- `selection.rs`: the note for open runs now says "Side does not apply to open runs - the tool stays on the run's air side, read from the part".
- Decision: `docs/decisions/1777-contour-open-run-side.md`.

The gouge gate is not changed. Before this fix, the post of the reported case was already blocked by the gouge gate. Now the program is correct, so the post is written.

## Readings (block 40 x 40 x 10 at the origin, 10 mm end mill, Z 10 to 0)

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| One open north edge, Side Auto / Inside / Outside | tool centre on y = 20; Gouge at moves 5, 6; post blocked ("program cuts below the model in 512 cell(s), worst 10.00 mm") | tool centre on y = 25; 0 warnings; post written (25 lines) |
| North and east edges | post blocked (960 cells) | tool stays 5 mm off the block; 0 warnings; post written (33 lines) |
| Closed rim | offset one radius out; post written | unchanged |
| Open run with Boundary area controls | refused by name | unchanged |

## How tested

Pinning tests:
- `camcraft-motion` lib, `machining2d::contour_run_side::tests` (8 tests): `an_open_edge_is_cut_one_radius_off_on_its_air_side`, `stock_to_leave_moves_the_tool_further_off`, `conventional_travels_the_air_side_the_other_way`, `a_run_with_material_on_both_sides_is_refused`, `a_run_whose_sides_change_between_levels_is_refused`, `a_run_that_ends_at_a_wall_is_refused`, `a_run_with_no_material_beside_it_rides_its_line`, `a_degenerate_run_is_refused_not_ridden`.
- `camcraft-app` new suite `contour_open_side`: `an_open_edge_of_a_part_is_cut_on_its_air_side_for_every_side`, `two_open_edges_turn_the_corner_on_their_air_side` (both also check that `posting::post_setup_unwritten` is Ok).
- `camcraft-app` `operations`: `an_open_run_contours_on_its_centerline` is renamed `an_open_run_contours_on_its_air_side` and now checks the offset ends. `a_mixed_pick_list_cuts_boundary_then_run_and_says_what_overlap_means` now checks that the run gives no Gouge warning (before, it checked that the centreline gouge was flagged).

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` is green on a3367c834 (motion lib + 48 motion suites ok in 328 s, app lib + 119 app suites ok in 750 s, 0 failed). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

No golden CL or NC file and no snapshot PNG changed.

- The maintainer's model `testdata/models/Block-w-slot.step` (not committed; the tests use the hand-built block of `area_support`).

title: fix(3d): a whole-model 3D Pocket clears an open-sided notch past its edge
body:
## What changed

A whole-model 3D Pocket used the model's silhouette as its footprint, and the level law erodes that by the tool radius. So the cutter's edge never passed the silhouette. On a notch open to the part's outside, the pocket left a band one radius wide along the open edges at the full stock height, and the op reported `ok` (#1749).

- `camcraft-motion`: new `machining3d::open_sides` (`machining3d/open_side.rs`). It grows the silhouette by the tool radius less 0.01 mm, minus a keep-out region. Where a level is open, the cutter centre now goes up to the silhouette edge. Where a level's material stands flush with the silhouette, the band is narrower than the erosion, so it cuts nothing there and a plain block gets no new ring.
- `camcraft-app`: the new `operation/open_side.rs` applies this footprint in the Pocket3D arm and in the Multi-Axis Rough arm (the stamped twin: one ladder). It applies only to the source-built footprint of an untilted whole-model source. A picked or Boundary-controlled region, and a tilted plane, stay as before. The keep-out is the silhouette of the setup's other parts.
- `keep_law::kept_models`: the setup's other parts now go into the solid law for Pocket3D and Multi-Axis Rough as a second net. This net also reports a cut through a second part that stands inside the model's own silhouette. Before, that cut read `ok` (the ladder's islands come only from its own model).
- `shared_face_bodies`: the #1706 pin (`the_sample_as_imported_refuses_the_3d_pocket_by_name`) pinned the old law. No 6 mm tool fit inside the 6.53 mm strip, so the op refused. Under the new law the pocket clears the stock beside the strip and verifies clean. The pin is renamed to `the_sample_as_imported_roughs_the_3d_pocket_beside_its_silhouette`. Recorded in `docs/decisions/1749-pocket3d-open-side.md`.

## How tested

New suite `crates/app/tests/pocket3d_open_side.rs`. The fixture is built in code: a 30 mm block with its +X+Y quadrant notched down to Z 20, in a stock that fits it in XY with its top at Z 32. The tool is a 10 mm flat end mill, with offset rings and shell on.
- `an_open_sided_notch_is_cleared_to_the_parts_edge`: measures the stock the path leaves (the lowest flat-end disc over each column) along both open edges, 0.05 mm inside the part edge. It must be at the floor, Z 20. It also checks that no feed disc enters the part's material at its Z, and that verify is clean. Before the fix, the stock stayed at Z 32.000 at (14.95, 10.80).
- `an_open_side_never_reaches_into_a_neighbouring_part`: a second part 1 mm past the +X open edge. No feed disc comes within R of it, verify is clean, and the +Y open edge is still cleared.
- `a_part_standing_in_the_notch_is_named_by_the_solid_law`: a second part on the notch floor, inside the model's silhouette, is reported (warnings > 0), not read as `ok`.

Mutation checks. Each mutation was reverted afterwards and the file compared byte-for-byte with its backup:
- `open_footprint` returns the region unchanged: the open-edge test fails (stock at Z 32.000).
- Keep-out made empty: the neighbour test fails (81 solid-law warnings; the second net fires).
- The `keep_law` line removed: the neighbour test and the solid-law test both fail.

Gates (Linux):
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the Pocket3D-only version of the change: motion suites ok. App suites ok except `operations::multiaxis_rough_peels_the_same_ladder_and_poses_its_walls` (150 vs 134 moves). That failure led to the Multi-Axis Rough change. The #1706 pin also failed there; it is updated as described above.
- After the final change, these targeted app suites, all green: operations, level_links, ribbon, suppressed_rest, rest_across_setups, stock_engine_agreement, setup_align, probe_op, remachining, drill_prior, area_controls, project_roundtrip, pocket3d_hsm, shared_face_bodies, keep_law, neighbour_law, kept_parts_live, coarse_laws, center_cut_multiaxis, pocket3d_open_side.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- The full quick gate was not re-run on the final head; only the targeted suites listed above were. The motion crate did not change after the quick gate's green motion run.
- No batch gate, heavy lanes, ui suites (`crates/ui/tests/operations.rs` uses Pocket3D) or snapshots.
- A tilted (3+2) 3D Pocket keeps the old silhouette law, so it can still leave the ridge.
- Stock that reaches more than about two radii past the silhouette is still not cleared by a whole-model 3D Pocket. That would be the stock-outline reading the 2D pocket has had since #12, which is a larger change. See the decision file.

Changelog: A whole-model 3D Pocket (and Multi-Axis Rough) clears a notch open to the part's outside past its open edge instead of leaving a tool-radius ridge, keeps off the setup's other parts, and warns when it cuts through one.

title: fix(2d): two open edges are a band the stock outline closes
body:
## What changed

- A selection of two open part edges is now a band for the pocket family (2D Offset, 2D Pocket, 2D Adaptive). Before, the selection was refused with "... is an open run - a 2D Offset cannot end mid-edge ...".
- The definition of the region is exact (`crates/app/src/operation/open_band.rs`, new):
  - Picked open runs that share an end are welded into one wall. Exactly two walls, A and B, must remain. Each wall is level. The two walls are at one height.
  - Each wall is run on straight along the tangent at each end.
  - S is the stock outline in XY, grown by the extension `e` with sharp corners.
  - `band(e) = (side of A that holds B) ∩ (side of B that holds A) ∩ S`.
- `band(0)` is the region of the selection. The pocket region law then removes the standing material of the part at each cut plane, as it does for a closed pick.
- `band(e)` is a lane. `boundary::resolve` clips the area to the lane after the extension step. Thus "Extend past" moves the open ends out of the stock along the edges. The extension does not make the band wider, and the tool does not go round the end of a wall.
- A selection with no clear band is refused by name:
  - no stock in the setup;
  - a wall that is not level, or walls at different heights;
  - walls at more than 45 degrees to each other, or walls that do not run alongside each other;
  - walls that cross or touch when run on, or that run together inside the stock;
  - a stock outline that does not cover the space between the walls, or that closes the band in more than one piece;
  - more than two walls, three edges at one point, open edges mixed with closed boundaries, an open edge of the stock;
  - tool containment On or Outside.
- One open edge keeps the old refusal, word for word. A tilted tool plane keeps the old refusal.
- No gouge check or collision check is changed. The band operation answers to the same section law and to the solid law against the other parts of the setup.
- The hooks are small: one call in `selection_geometry_in` (`selection.rs`), one clip in `boundary::resolve`, one field in `AreaCtx`. `stitch::gather_runs` is now `pub(super)`.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1735-open-edge-band.md` (the definition and the options dropped).
- No new command, thus no new MCP tool.

## Readings

Fixture: a 40 x 40 x 20 block with a 16 mm slot (|x| <= 8) down to Z 10, in a 70 x 70 stock, 10 mm tool. The readings are the same for the three kinds.

- Extension 0: the tool centre stays in |x| <= 3 and goes to y = ±30 (the tool edge is at the stock edge). 0 warnings.
- Extension 7: the tool centre goes to y = ±37 and stays in |x| <= 3. 0 warnings.
- Bottom at Z 5 (below the slot floor): cuts occur only at |y| >= 25, outside the part.
- A second part ("clamp") in the open end of the band: the operation has `Warning::Gouge` findings, and the post is refused with "post blocked - gouge: program cuts below the model in 156 cell(s)". No file is written.

## How tested

Pinning tests in `crates/app/tests/open_band.rs`:
- `two_open_slot_edges_cut_the_band_up_to_the_stock_edge`
- `the_extension_moves_the_open_ends_out_of_the_stock_along_the_walls`
- `a_bottom_under_the_slot_floor_never_cuts_the_part`
- `a_selection_with_no_clear_band_is_refused_by_name`
- `with_no_stock_nothing_closes_the_band`
- `the_selection_account_names_the_band`
- `a_band_pass_that_cuts_another_part_blocks_the_post` (expects the refusal)

Unit tests in `crates/app/src/operation/open_band_tests.rs`:
- `the_band_is_the_strip_between_the_walls_closed_by_the_stock`
- `unclear_walls_are_refused_by_name`
- `runs_that_share_an_end_weld_into_one_wall`

The unit test found one defect during the work: two walls on one line gave half of the stock as the band. A touch check now refuses that selection, and the test pins it.

Gate (Windows): 
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` on commit c18717ddf: app suites ok (1509 s, the lib tests and 190 suites, because the gate map names `app::operation`), ui suites ok (141 s), 0 failed.
- The head commit 106ceb692 changes only `open_band.rs` for clippy (explicit NaN tests, a type alias). After it: `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean, `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test open_band` passes (7 tests), and the 3 unit tests pass. The full quick gate was not run again on the head commit.

No golden file and no snapshot changed.

## Not exercised

- The real model `Block-w-slot.step`. It is not a tracked file. The tests use a synthetic slotted block.
- The GUI. No test clicks the two edges in the viewport.
- Curved walls and walls of a STEP tessellation. The fixture walls are straight.
- A tilted setup and turned stock.
- Linux and macOS, the batch tier and the release tier.
- A merge with draft PR #1756 (issue 1727, the open boundary path). `git merge-tree` of this head with head 52e4c70c gives no conflict. The merged tree was not built.

## Limits

- With extension 0 the tool centre stops one tool radius inside the stock edge. An extension of one tool radius or more clears the stock edge.
- A blind slot picked as one U-shaped run stays refused as one open run. Follow-up: #1762.
- Walls that meet inside the stock (a wedge with one open end) are refused by name. Follow-up: #1763.

Changelog: A 2D Offset, 2D Pocket or 2D Adaptive with two opposite open edges selected now cuts the band between the edges up to the stock edge, and the extension moves the open ends out of the stock along the edges; an unclear selection is refused by name.

title: fix(boundary): edges bound the cut in any pick mode, two edges keep the area between them
body:
## What changed

- **Edge picks reach the Boundary group in any pick mode** (`crates/ui/src/feature_click.rs`). An armed boundary row took the toolbar's pick kinds, so in Faces mode (the usual one) a click on an edge picked the face, and no edge could bound the cut. It now takes faces and edges whatever the mode. Points stay refused by name, as before.
- **Two or more separate edges bound the area between them** (`crates/geometry/src/boundary_chains.rs`, new; one arm in `boundary::resolve`). The open boundary may hold separate open chains. Each chain splits the stock the way a single chain does (`sides_of_chain`). Each keeps the side that holds the operation's own area, and the area kept is the area between the chains. A face bounded by two of its edges is faced between them, and the rows run on past the face at the open ends. Face lays its rows along the first chain. Side B keeps everything beyond the chains.
- **Refused by name, never guessed** (each pinned and mutation-checked, below):
  - chains that touch or cross ("chains i and j touch or cross");
  - a chain with the operation's area evenly on both sides;
  - a Contour given two chains ("a Contour rides one open chain");
  - an include / exclude made of separate chains: the Apply door, as for one open chain (`PickShape::is_open` covers the new `PickShape::Chains`).
- The old refusal "the boundary picks spell N separate open runs" is gone. The maintainer asked for exactly that case to work. The `area_picks.rs` assertion that pinned it now pins two chains.
- Everything is a command: the picks go into the page draft, and Apply commits them as the existing undoable `EditOperationParams::with_area`. Over MCP, `set_operation_area`'s `open.picks` takes edge chain ids. It already accepted them; a test now pins it. The issue names `set_operation_geometry`, but that tool sets the operation's source and not its boundary. The decision file records this.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1727-boundary-edges.md`.

## How tested

Pinning tests:
- UI: `egui_app::tests::edge_click_modifiers::an_armed_boundary_row_takes_edges_in_faces_mode`. In Faces mode, with the row armed, a viewport click on an edge takes the edge, and a Ctrl+click adds a second separate edge ("2 open chains"). Apply commits both edges, and undo takes them back out.
- Toolpath: `area_chains::a_face_bounded_by_two_of_its_edges_is_faced_between_them`. Face on the block's top with its north and south rim edges as the boundary: every feed has its tool edge within y +-20, works up to both edges, and runs past the face at both open ends. The verify is silent (0 warnings).
- Refusals: `area_chains::chains_that_cross_are_refused_by_name`, `area_chains::a_contour_cannot_ride_two_separate_chains`, `area_chains::an_include_of_two_separate_chains_is_refused_at_apply` (this one also checks one undoable edit and its undo), `boundary_chains::tests::the_area_lies_between_the_chains_and_a_tie_is_refused`, `boundary_chains::tests::runs_group_into_chains_and_touching_chains_are_refused`.
- MCP: `mcp_pick::edges_set_as_the_open_boundary_ride_one_undo_step`.

Mutation check: each refusal line was deleted (or neutralised), the named test was confirmed red, then the line was restored, the file touched, and `cmp` run against a backup:
- touch check in `touching_refusal`: `chains_that_cross_are_refused_by_name` red;
- its call site in `picks_geom`: `chains_that_cross_are_refused_by_name` red;
- the tie check in `sides_of_chains`: `the_area_lies_between_the_chains_and_a_tie_is_refused` red;
- the Contour arm in `contour_open::open_run`: `a_contour_cannot_ride_two_separate_chains` red;
- `PickShape::Chains` in `is_open` (the Apply door): `an_include_of_two_separate_chains_is_refused_at_apply` red;

The winding/import code, test, and STL fixture are unchanged from the reviewed head. The boundary suites and mutation checks passed. The full UI suite and clippy for all touched crates passed with `--all-targets -- -D warnings`.

## Not exercised

- Release-only slow suites, release pixel snapshots, and Windows.
- The viewport's boundary overlay does not draw separate chains. The page lists the entry as "N edges, M open chains".

Branched from upstream/main 0db66c44, which none of the open Geometry-tab PRs (#1701, #1710, #1711) collide with: this PR does not touch `geo_page.rs`.

- Allowed cross drill (`OpParams::Drill { cross, .. }`) in `fidelity_law::excess_aware`.
- Grew `cross_stock::standoff` radii and Z tops by `band_growth(excess)`.
- Expanded `cross_entry::tube_max` facet slabs along normals by `s + grow` for `entry_grown` and `tube_reach`.
- Added `part_grow` to `drill_reach::cross_reach` when `st.raw` is `None`.
- Grew `drill_station::material`, `drill_reach::cross_holder_excess`, and `band_clear` Z bands and radii by `band_growth(excess)`.

- Tightened `camcraft_sim::verify::rapids_radial::radial_rapids` with `band_growth()` on `stock_top_z` and `tightened(...)` on disc radius.
- Recorded the design choice in `docs/decisions/1053-fidelity-cross-drill.md`.

## Cause
PR #1081 lifted probe and plasma on coarse models, leaving cross drill refused because its construction laws (`cross_stock`, `cross_entry`, `drill_reach`, `drill_station`), solid law (`cross_part`), and radial rapid law (`rapids_radial`) did not account for model excess.

title: fix(pick): the pick door takes an edge pick whose stitched ring has no area
body:
## What changed

The first Ctrl+click on a second edge did not add the edge in some views. The cause is the pick door of the pocket family (2D Pocket, 2D Adaptive, 2D Offset), not the list.

- The stitcher welds open edge runs where their ends meet when you look from above.
- One vertical edge, or an edge together with the edge below it, becomes a ring that has no area.
- The pick door (`operation::selection_refusal`) refused that selection with "the stitched rim of ... projects to a line from above and bounds no area".
- Thus a plain click on a vertical edge selected nothing, and the next Ctrl+click gave only one edge. A Ctrl+click on the edge below the first edge added nothing.

The door now accepts a selection when the refusal is the collapse of a ring that only the stitcher closed. The operation stores the picks. Generate gives the same refusal as before. The Geometry page continues to show the sentence below the picks.

The door continues to refuse a wall face pick and a closed chain on a wall. The stitcher and the toolpath code did not change. The constant `STITCHED_RIM` now gives the ring label at the two stitch sites.

## Readings

On the model `Block-w-slot` with a 2D Offset operation and Pick armed for edges:

- Orthographic Top view: 0 incorrect pairs of 56 (click A, Ctrl+click B).
- Perspective view: 136 incorrect pairs of 240 before the fix. Each incorrect pair had the refusal above in the status line.
- The list rows and the chips were always equal to the stored selection. The list did not hide an edge.

## How it was tested

- `crates/app/tests/pick_doors.rs`: `edge_picks_that_meet_only_from_above_pass_the_pick_door` (new). It failed before the fix and it passes now. The other 7 tests of the suite pass.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/first_ctrl_click.rs` (new, real viewport clicks in a perspective view): `the_first_ctrl_click_adds_the_edge_under_the_first_one` and `a_plain_click_takes_an_upright_edge_and_ctrl_click_adds_to_it`. They expect two edges in the operation, two rows in the list and two chips, and one undo removes one pick. The two tests failed without the fix and pass with it.

- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib -- first_ctrl_click edge_click_modifiers footer_tests geo_ pick`: 118 pass.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## What was not exercised

- A hand test in the GUI. An agent cannot start the application.
- Before and after screenshots. An agent cannot make them. The maintainer must add them or accept the PR without them.
- A Ctrl+click during which the pointer moves more than 4 px. That input starts a box selection and makes no click pick. It is a possible second cause of a lost Ctrl+click and it did not change.
- Operation kinds other than 2D Offset and 2D Pocket in the new tests.
- The batch gate and the release gate.

The toolpath for such a selection is the subject of issue 1735 and did not change here.

title: fix(tools): assemble modular multi-piece tool bodies (#361)
body:
## What changed

`ToolBody` now stores an ordered `pieces: Vec<BodyPiece>` table while keeping `facets` and `frame` as the merged body. Each piece records its label, facet count, rigid placement, and transformed STEP coordinate systems (`BodyCsys`).

`tool_body_assembly` and `tool_body_mate` load piece files, mate child `MCS` frames onto parent `CSW*` frames (or explicit named parent and child frames), enforce the facet budget, and rebuild merged facets cleanly. Ambiguous, missing, mismatched, or single-piece-removal inputs fail with named error messages.

`SetToolBody::attach_piece`, `SetToolBody::attach_loaded_piece`, and `SetToolBody::remove_piece` update modular assemblies in one undoable command step. `ToolBodyDto` serializes `pieces` additively and omits the key for single-piece bodies without CSYS metadata.

MCP tools `attach_tool_body_piece` and `remove_tool_body_piece`, `get_tool_body` (`pieces`), and the Tool Editor Modular Assembly section expose piece attachment and removal to agents and users.

## Cause

Single-piece tool body replacement discarded prior pieces when a user attached a clamping unit, extension, or modular lathe head from vendor STEP/STL/OBJ files. No CSYS mating or piece tracking existed to align multi-piece assemblies or judge them together in simulation.

title: feat(wcs): store WCS axis flips (Flip X/Y/Z); refuse post and generation by name
body:
Stacked on #1717 (base `issue/1648-wcs-page-work-offset`). Retarget this PR to `main` before #1717 merges.

## What changed

Part 1 of issue 1649 ("Split in two"): the WCS page can store a flipped axis. This PR does not change posted G-code.

- **Stored flags.** A new component `schema::WcsFlip([bool; 3])` is on the setup's WCS entity. "No flip" is stored as no component.
- **One undoable command.** `SetWcsFlip::for_setup` sets the flags of a setup's WCS. It refuses an unknown setup by name. If the WCS was never placed, it places it at the identity, and undo removes it again.
- **WCS page.** Three toggles, "Flip X", "Flip Y" and "Flip Z", are under the quarter turns. A lit toggle is a flipped axis. When an axis is flipped, a note tells the user that posting and generating are refused until the flip is cleared.
- **Viewport triad.** A flipped axis is drawn in the opposite direction. A flipped WCS at the origin does not hide the world axes.
- **Refusal by name.** The post verification gate and the generation door (`collect_job`) refuse a flipped WCS. An example message: "the WCS (G54) has its X axis flipped; posting or generating with a flipped WCS is not available yet - clear the flip on the WCS page (operations: Face1)". All post paths use the gate, so no path posts with a flip set.
- **Project file v62.** A WCS row can have the optional key `flip` (`{"x": true}`), and only flipped axes are written. A file without the key opens with no flip. A `flip` key on a row that is not a WCS is refused as corrupt.
- **Undo keeps the flip.** `DeleteEntity`, `DeleteSetup` and the datum transfer of `CreateSetup` keep the flip.
- **MCP.** A new tool, `set_wcs_flip {x?, y?, z?, setup?}`. An axis that is not given keeps its flag. `get_job` shows `setups[].wcs.flip`. The camcraft-mcp skill has the tool row and a "Shipped" line.
- **Decisions.** `docs/decisions/1720-wcs-flip-flags.md`.

## How tested

- `crates/app/tests/wcs_flip.rs` (new, 10 tests). It pins these points:
  - the command, undo and redo;
  - the refusal of an unknown setup;
  - the post refusal by name, and the same stream after the flip is cleared;
  - the generation refusal by name;
  - the setup name in the message;
  - DeleteSetup and DeleteEntity undo;
  - the datum transfer;
  - the project round trip, an old file, and a corrupt row;

- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/wcs_flip_tests.rs` (new, 3 tests). It pins the toggle layout and live state, the click to the command, the reversed triad, undo and redo, and the status line.
- The existing suites `wcs_page_tests`, `wcs_gizmo_tests` and `wcs_circle_tests` pass.

A file that I wrote into the worktree during the run made the gate VOID before its ui step. Then I ran the same ui step command by hand on the same tree, and it passed (lib 778 tests and 12 suites).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised

- No before/after screenshots: this worker cannot start the GUI. The maintainer must add them before `/merge-ready` offers the PR.
- Posting with a flip (part 2 of issue 1649) is not in this PR. There are no NC golden changes.
- No script verb. The decision file gives the reason.

title: fix(post): Tormach lathe G76 J makes LinuxCNC's R1 ladder cut the record's passes
body:
## What changed

`assets/posts/tormach-lathe.cps`, `g76Grid`: J (first depth) is no longer floored to the grid on its own. LinuxCNC's G76 with `R1` cuts J, 2J, ... with the last pass clamped at K, so the control cuts ceil(K/J) passes. The record lays n = ceil(height / first depth) equal rungs (g76Why already holds the equal ladder), so J must satisfy (n-1)J < K <= nJ:

- J is the shallower grid rounding (as before) when that keeps the count;
- when the shallower J would add a pass, J is the one grid step up, and never a full grid step over the record's first cut;
- otherwise the record is refused by name: `G76 threading cycle refused - no first depth J on the control's grid makes R1's equal ladder cut the record's n passes (K ...)`.

The root keeps its outward rounding. Peak, root, I and K are unchanged.

## Golden change, line by line

title: fix(import): load a STEP closed shell that meshes open as an incomplete model
body:
## What changed

A STEP closed shell that meshes open (a real gap, e.g. walls missing on a face truck cannot mesh) used to be refused at import (#1576), so the part could not even be loaded for viewing or setup. Now the model import lands it **incomplete**:

- `step_closed::judge` returns the hole, named, instead of refusing; `step::parse_open` and `import::{load,parse}_model_open_within` keep it in `Graded::open`. Every other loader (`load_model`, `parse_model`, `*_graded_within`: fixtures-by-path, tool bodies) still refuses with the same words as before.
- `ImportModel` (GUI, MCP `import_model`, script `import`) lands the mesh with the fidelity-unknown sentinel (`model_fidelity::UNKNOWN_MM`, #1056) and the hole in a new component `schema::MeshOpen`. The sentinel rides every chord path (stock copies, setup clones, undo, save), so every operation on the model and the program verdict are refused at the post by the existing gate, and the program sim gives no verdict.
- New module `mesh_open`: the refusal words ("model 'X' was imported incomplete - closed shell #N (F faces) meshes open: ... - so it has walls missing and no gouge check against it can be trusted; re-export the model, or import an STL"), the model page / import status line ("Incomplete: ..."), and the MCP/script `reduced_fidelity` facts (`incomplete: true`, `hole`).
- The hole is traded by `UpdateModel` (new `with_hole`, undo restores it; a whole re-import clears it), `DeleteEntity` undo, and the project file (optional entity key `mesh_open`, written only beside `fidelity_unknown`; a `mesh_open` without the mark is refused as corrupt). No project version bump: an old reader drops the key and keeps the mark, so it still refuses (decision file).
- `model_fidelity::set` clears any hole, so a stale hole never speaks for a whole mesh.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/1610-open-shell-incomplete.md`.

## How tested

Pinning tests, new suite `crates/app/tests/import_step_open_shell.rs`:

- `the_hole_rides_the_project_file_and_is_refused_without_its_mark`

title: fix(ui): keep the near plane and the ortho eye consistent with the zoom
body:
### Summary

A viewport fix for the way the camera eats the model from the inside.

Two ways the camera clipped the model while zooming:

- **Perspective:** the near plane was a fixed 0.1 mm from the eye, so at close zoom the geometry right in front of the near plane clipped instead of rendering — zooming in went through the model. The near plane now rides `dist` (0.1 % of the view depth, clamped to 1e-5 min and 0.1 max).
- **Orthographic:** `dist` moved the eye, so zooming dollied the eye into the model and clipped through its faces from inside. The eye now sits at a fixed nominal distance (100 mm) behind the target, and `dist` is only a zoom factor for the view box's half-height — the way it was always meant to work. The near plane now reaches far behind the eye plane: `-((dist * 20.0).max(1000.0) - ORTHO_EYE_DIST)`.

Changelog: UI — the perspective near plane moves with the dolly distance and the orthographic camera's near plane no longer clips through geometry while zooming.

The tests pin the new ortho depth formula and a point in front of the eye plane (`dist = 300`, 150 mm back from the target), asserting it stays inside the clip volume.

### Verification

`cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` — 803 passed. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets` — clean. No posted G-code, collision check, stock simulation math or geometry changed.

No issue covers this viewport bug yet — a maintainer will file one.

title: fix(post): Tormach lathe moves one axis at a time after G30 and leaves the stock before it
body:
## What changed

`assets/posts/tormach-lathe.cps` only. The mill post `tormach.cps` does not change.

LinuxCNC's G30 moves every axis in one straight line to the stored position (params 5181-5189). The operator stores that position, so the post cannot know where the line goes. Before this change, the first rapid after `G30` went diagonally to the start point, and the closing `G30` went diagonally from the last retract. Now:

- **After G30** (tool change, or a "home" after-operation), the first point is approached one axis at a time:
  - The point is outside the stock's diameter (all turning and threading starts): `G0 X`, then `G0 Z`.
  - The point is inside the diameter, in front of the face (a hole on centre): `G0 Z`, then `G0 X`. A point ON the face goes to the section's `ClearancePlane` first, then X, then Z down to the point.
  - Any other point: refused by name.
- **Before G30** (tool change, "home", program end): `G0 X` out to the stock's diameter, then `G0 Z` out to the face (or to the `ClearancePlane` when the corner is not clear in either axis). The lines go before the next section's notes and work offset word, because they are in the old frame.
- **Stock and planes** come from the stream's own `StockXY*`, `StockZTop` and `ClearancePlane` PARAMs. No margin is added by the post.
- **Refused by name:** no stock box; a first point inside the stock with no `ClearancePlane` in front of the face; a section that ends inside the stock's envelope; a section that ends on the stock's corner with no `ClearancePlane`; a feed, arc or thread half-turn as the first motion after G30.

**Order chosen:** X first, then Z, for every point outside the stock's diameter. For a hole on centre, X first from a G30 beside the bar moves into the bar, and a clearance diameter is not stated in the stream. Z first to the stated `ClearancePlane` needs no guess, so the post uses it there. The reasons are in `docs/decisions/1604-lathe-g30-rapid.md`.

## How tested

New suite `crates/app/tests/lathe_post_tormach_g30.rs` (each pin mutation-checked; seven mutations of the post, each one fails at least one pin):

- `the_first_move_after_g30_is_x_alone_then_z_alone`: turning and G76 threading programs go `G0 X..` then `G0 Z..` after each G30; the hole goes `G0 Z30`, `G0 X0`, `G0 Z20`.
- `the_departure_goes_plus_x_then_plus_z_before_g30`: the hole ends `G0 X20` before G30; a section behind the face leaves `G0 Z10` before the next tool change, before the next work offset word.
- `no_stored_g30_outside_the_stock_is_reached_across_it`: for a 41 x 41 grid of stored G30 positions outside the stock, no G30 line and no added rapid crosses the stock (turning, hole and thread programs). The first move from every G30 is one axis, and every G30 line starts at the stock's outer corner.
- `a_missing_stock_or_clearance_is_refused_by_name`: no stock, no clearance plane in front of the face, an end on the corner with no clearance, an end inside the envelope, and a feed first after G30.

Mutations: radial approach Z-then-X; the old diagonal approach; no departure; departure without +Z; departure without +X; no clearance refusal; no stock refusal.

**Goldens:** the eight `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach-lathe/*.nc` and the recorded `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/tormach-lathe/tool_change.nc` were regenerated. A script checked each diff: the first two-axis `G0` after each `G30` becomes one-axis `G0` lines that end at the same point; the lines added before a `G30` are one-axis `+X` or `+Z` moves; every other line is the same and in the same order. Result: GOLDEN DIFF OK (12 approaches split, 5 departures added). I also mutated a golden two ways (a changed F word, a changed end point) and the script failed both.

Hand-built test streams in `lathe_post_tormach`, `lathe_post_tormach_thread` and `lathe_cycle_exit` now state a stock (`tormach_lathe_support::stock_params`), because the post refuses a stream with no stock. title: fix(motion): circular ramp entry rides the ring at the ramp angle

A Circular with `entry: ramp` did not ramp at its ramp angle. The cause is the legacy ramp chord. The chord goes from the tool's XY to the pass start. A ring starts and ends at the same point. Thus at each level change the chord has no length: the tool fed straight down at the cutting feed (500), with no note. The first entry of the inner ring was a 76 deg chord from the outer ring. The first entry of the outer ring was an axial dive.

The fix is one match arm in `descent::plan_arm` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/descent.rs`). On the circular kernel (`Motion::ring_zig`), the Ramp arm now plans the zig-zag ramp along the ring. It uses `ramp_fallback`, the same path as the helix's stand-down. The angle is the transition's ramp angle (3 deg by default). The ramp rides the ring's arcs (`push_zig_ring`, #1558). If the ring is too short for the angle, the descent is a dive at the plunge feed with the note `entry: the ring is too short to ramp at the angle - axial dive on the floor instead at (...)`.

The arm applies only to the circular kernel. Other ladders (pocket, contour, bore) do not change. This change does not touch `ring.rs` (no overlap with PR #1651).

Decision: `docs/decisions/1609-circular-ramp-angle.md`.

## How tested

New suite `crates/motion/tests/circular_ramp_angle.rs`, on the #1558 repro with `entry: ramp`, climb and conventional:
- `a_ramp_entry_circular_never_descends_steeper_than_its_ramp_angle`: each descending feed move is at most 3 deg (measured along the arc), or it is an axial move at the plunge feed with an `entry:` note.
- `every_ring_level_of_the_ramp_entry_is_entered_by_the_ramp`: no axial descent on this hole.

Both tests are red on upstream main (an axial feed at 500 at (-34.0, 2.9, -1.508); 25 axial descents).

Mutation checks (each one red, then reverted):
- The arm always substitutes: both tests red.
- The substitution dives at the cutting feed: both tests red.
- `ramp_fallback` doubles the angle: the angle test red.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green (motion lib, center_cut_law, circular_ramp_angle, entry_approach, level_links, predrilled_entry, xy_arc_entry; app bore_entry, ladder_entry_height). Also green: motion `circular_arcs`; app `arc_entry`, `circular_arcs`, `circular_pick_law`, `circular_entity_law`, `circle_centre`, `circular_pick`, `golden_cl`, `mill2d_b`, `operations`, `pocket_recognition`, `units_in_refusals`, `stock_source_law`. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## Goldens

No golden moves. No committed golden uses a Circular with `entry: ramp` (`circular_ring_arcs.cl` uses Helix; `sinker_orbit_circular.cl` is the sinker orbit). Posted G-code of a Circular with `entry: ramp` changes: the straight feeds and the steep chord become helical ramp arcs at 3 deg.

## Not exercised

- Other ladders with closed passes (pocket offset rings, bore) and a Ramp entry with no angle set: not checked for the same straight chord.
- Batch and release tiers.

Changelog: Circular with entry Ramp now ramps along the ring at the ramp angle (3 deg by default) at every level, or dives at the plunge feed with a note; before, it fed straight down at the cutting feed (#1609)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fork synced at upstream/main 2b6e03f2.

Fixes #1609

title: fix(motion): a chord that grazes one piece's wall and leaves the area no longer clears
body:
## What changed

- `chord_clears` moved from `slots.rs` to the new `crates/motion/src/machining2d/chord_clear.rs` (`slots.rs` re-exports it).
- The law splits the chord at each loop vertex that the chord touches without a crossing. The midpoint of each piece must be in the closed region. Before, one midpoint decided the full chord.

## The cause

The part pinches the band between the part and the stock. Thus, the cutter-centre area has pieces whose walls are on one line (Y -32, the offset edge of the stock). The old law found no edge that crossed the chord from (-8.05, -32) to (32, -32), and it read one midpoint, which was in a piece. Thus, the 2D Adaptive path fed along Y -32 at each level, 0.94 mm into the part.

The issue gives "10 mm at (-1.44, -29.94)". That value comes from the stock in the first report: its top is at Z 10, and the top of the part is at Z 20. The sim reads each part column above the stock as a 10 mm gouge, and (-1.44, -29.94) is the first part column. The pin uses a stock that covers the part.

## How tested

- `crates/app/tests/adaptive_pinch.rs`:
  - `a_whole_model_clearing_never_joins_two_corners_across_the_part_that_pinches_them`: a 20 mm disc in a 31 mm stock. 2D Adaptive and 2D Offset, aligned and turned stock. The cutter stays off the disc, and the op has no warnings.
  - `the_users_part_with_default_adaptive_keeps_the_cutter_off_it` (heavy lane, about 5 min in debug): `Milling-test.step` in a 70 x 70 x 27 box on Z -7, 2D Adaptive seed params, through `GenerateOperation` (`operation::generate`). Aligned and turned stock: the cutter reaches less than 0.06 mm into the part section at each Z, and the op has 0 warnings. Aligned stock: `simulate_document` has 0 gouge cells.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/chord_clear.rs`: two unit tests (a chord across the gap between two pieces does not clear; a graze along one wall clears).
- Mutation: with the old midpoint law, all three pins fail ("reaches 0.936 into the part" at (1.963, -32.000, 15.000); "0.479 into the disc"; the gap chord clears). A first draft also split the chord at the ends of collinear edges. With that branch removed, all pins pass, so I removed it (the vertex split does that work).
- Quick gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green (motion suites 145 s, app suites 209 s, 0 failed). It includes `golden_cl` and `solid_law_goldens`. No golden moved.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- The pin uses an end mill with 30 mm flutes. With the catalog's 15 mm flutes, the 25 mm deep part gives `ShankHit` warnings at the lower levels. That refusal is correct and is not part of this issue.
- The sim pin runs only on the aligned stock. The program sim does not run on the turned stock; the op check covers it.
- The keep law of #1615 is not on main, so this PR does not run it.

Decision: `docs/decisions/1620-chord-pieces.md`.

The branch is based on c00ba18a and merges upstream/main 3ead1295.

Changelog: A 2D clearing no longer feeds across the part between two pieces of the cutter area whose walls are on one line (whole-model 2D Adaptive on Milling-test.step cut 0.94 mm into the part).

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1620

title: feat(ui): drag a part along an axis with move handles (#1198 b)
body:
#1198 slice (b): move handles with drag-to-move. Slice (a), the bottom bar, merged in #1203.

**GUI hand check needed.** The handles, the drag feel and the readout were tested only through the kittest harness and headless state tests. Nobody has looked at them on screen yet.

## What changed
- **Move mode in the bottom bar.** A seventh bar button (a four-armed cross) turns `State::move_handles` on and off. It is off by default, it is view state like pick-through, and it queues no command.
- **Handles** (`crates/ui/src/move_drag.rs`, painted by `crates/ui/src/egui_app/move_handles.rs`). With Move on and exactly one shown part selected, three arms in the axis colours start at the part's bounding-box centre and each ends in a ball. The arms stay 70 px long on screen at any zoom. The ball under the pointer is drawn larger.
- **Drag.** Pressing a ball takes the press before orbit and pick. Empty space still orbits. While the button is down, the preview slides the body along the axis (`world.rs` draws it offset) and never writes the world. The signed distance shows just above the bar. The distance is where the cursor ray comes closest to the axis line, so the part stays under the cursor in perspective and in ortho.
- **One command per drag.** The release queues `CommandKind::MoveModelBy { name, delta }`. The drain (`crates/ui/src/state_move_by.rs`) runs it as the Model page's own `MoveModel::new`, with the rotation copied bit for bit. That means one undo step, the same staleness, the same following stock and the same fixture-clash warning as a typed move. No new placement path.
- **What adds no history step:** Escape during a drag (the key is consumed), a drag that ends where it began, and turning Move off.
- **Turned setups.** When the active setup holds the part turned (#326), the drag happens in that setup's frame. The shown delta is rotated back into the document frame, so the part moves along the axis the user sees.
- Decisions are in `docs/decisions/1198-drag-to-move.md`: only parts are dragged in this slice, Move mode is off by default, and the preview moves the body only.

## MCP
No new app command, so no new MCP tool. `MoveModelBy` is a UI queue verb over the existing `MoveModel`, and the MCP `move_model` tool already places a part through `MoveModel`. An agent can make every move a drag makes.

## How tested
- `egui_app::tests::body_drag` (kittest, the real shell; 5 tests):
  - `handles_show_only_in_move_mode_on_a_selected_part`: a ball per axis, constant size when zoomed out, gone when Move is off.
  - `a_ball_drag_is_one_undoable_move_by_the_dragged_distance`: the preview never writes the world; the release moves the part by the dragged distance along X only; one undo returns the history to clean.
  - `escape_mid_drag_cancels_with_no_history_step`
  - `a_drag_that_ends_where_it_began_adds_nothing`: also checks that a press on a ball is not a pick.
  - `empty_space_still_orbits_in_move_mode`
- `move_drag_tests` (headless state; 5 tests):
  - `the_drag_distance_is_the_axis_point_under_the_cursor`: 12.5 mm along Y; one queued command.
  - `a_press_off_the_balls_is_not_a_drag`
  - `a_turned_setup_moves_the_part_along_the_axis_it_shows`
  - `the_rotation_is_kept_bit_for_bit`
  - `a_non_finite_distance_is_refused_by_name`
- The existing bar laws hold with the seventh button: `viewport_bar::tests::bar_fits_its_buttons` and `law_tests::view_cube_tests::the_hud_is_laid_out_from_the_pane_alone`, which iterates every button in `NAVS`.
- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): ui lib plus the boundary, boundary_picks, feedback, fixtures, gpu_render, machine, models, operations, shell and theme_files suites. 752 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised
- The handles have not been seen on a real screen, and real mouse input has not been tried. GUI hand check needed.
- The bar is wider now, so the viewport pixel goldens differ. They are regenerated at the cut; no PNG is changed here.
- Fixtures and the stock are not draggable (recorded decision).

## Left on #1198
- (c) rotate handles.
- (d) snapping with a modifier key, and typed values in the bar.

Fork synced at v0.18.0; upstream/main merged into the branch.

title: feat(edm): wire taper by angle word - the control's corner rule as machine data
body:
fork synced at v0.19.0.

## What changed

A wire EDM can now state an **angle-word taper dialect** in place of U/V moves. The control's behaviour goes in the machine file as data, so the verify can judge the lean the control will actually cut.

- **Machine data** (`post::machine::edm_taper`, new): `edm.taper_angle { positive: top_left|top_right, corner: mitre|cone }`. Both values are enumerated words with no default. A garbled word refuses the file. An unstated one is refused by name at generation. The angle code is `edm.codes.taper_angle`, a template with `{angle}`.
- **Generator** (`motion::wire_edm::taper`): a `WireCorner` rule.
  - `Mitre` is #536's path. On the fixture its CL equals #536's golden byte for byte (pinned).
  - `Cone` pivots the wire about each top-plane corner and holds the lean at the angle. The lower end runs on an arc of radius `H tan a`, laid as posed moves at most 2 degrees apart.
  - Under `cone`, a lead-in that meets a corner is refused by name.
- **Door** (`app::operation::wire_op::corner_rule`): a U/V machine keeps the mitre. An angle-word machine uses its stated rule. An incomplete rule is refused by name, and so is a 4-axis cut, because one angle cannot state two profiles. The rule is stamped only for angle-word machines, so U/V stamps do not change.
- **Post** (`app::posting_wire::angled`, `wire-iso.cps`):
  - Each move's X Y is written on the programmed plane, which is the work's top. The angle word is passed as `PARAM WireAngle`, signed by the side rule and computed from the path. No U/V words are written.
  - The cone's turning moves are not sent, because the control makes them itself.
  - `taper_on` and the angle word are written before the lead-in, and `taper_off` before the lead-out.
  - A machine that states neither `uv` nor `edm.taper_angle` is refused by name.
  - The new PARAMs are listed in `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md`.
- The decision record is `docs/decisions/1164-wire-taper-angle-word.md`.

## How tested

- `crates/app/tests/wire_taper_angle.rs` (new):
  - `an_angle_word_punch_posts_its_golden_with_the_mitre_rule`: new NC golden `tests/golden/nc/wire-iso/wire_taper_angle_punch.nc`; the CL equals `wire_taper_punch.cl`; the sign flips under `top_right`.
  - `the_cone_rule_turns_the_wire_about_each_corner`: the lean is held at 3 degrees through every corner, and the NC equals the mitre golden except for the note line.
  - `a_corner_the_stated_rule_gouges_blocks_the_post`: on a 3-degree drafted punch with sharp corners, the mitre rule verifies clean and posts. The cone rule's rounded lower corners gouge it, so the post is blocked with `wire gouge`.
  - `an_incomplete_dialect_and_a_four_axis_angle_cut_are_refused_by_name`: a missing corner rule, a missing side rule, neither uv nor angle, and 4-axis on an angle machine.
- `motion` unit test `the_cone_rule_holds_the_lean_and_refuses_a_lead_into_a_corner`; `post` unit test `taper_angle_words_parse_and_garbled_ones_refuse_the_file`.
- U/V goldens: `wire_taper`, `wire_4axis`, `wire_post`, `wire_contour` and `wire_verify` pass with their goldens unedited.
- Merge-time refresh (merge of upstream main df90b031, head 9673a77e): `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green (3 steps, 0 failed, 21.1 min; 3215 tests passed); `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; golden `wire_taper_angle_punch.nc` unchanged.
- Gate on the pre-refresh head 39d014d8: `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/537-wire-4axis` green (3 steps, 0 failed, 11.2 min); the wire suites by hand (wire_taper 5, wire_4axis 6, wire_post 5, wire_contour 7, wire_verify 3, wire_taper_angle 4: all pass); `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## Not exercised

- No real EDM control (D10). The angle code and dialect words are invented on the synthetic fixture.
- How a real control ramps the lean over the lead-in and lead-out is modelled as a linear ramp, the same as #536. The decision record states this.
- The `arc` corner rule (lean change rounded over a stated radius) is not offered.
- No UI page field for `edm.taper_angle`. It is machine-file data only, like `edm.codes`.

Changelog: Wire EDM: a machine can state an angle-word taper dialect (edm.taper_angle: side rule and mitre/cone corner rule). The wire post writes the angle word, and the verify judges the lean the stated corner rule cuts.

### Review fixes at b1c287a0 (the mutation check on 9673a77e)
Tests only, plus one behaviour-neutral extraction: the angle-word lean in `posting_wire::stream` moved into `angle_lean()` so its three door-shadowed refusals can be unit-tested. No golden or snapshot changed. Each line below was deleted (or neutralised) and its test went RED, then went GREEN again once the line was restored.

| Line (review) | Mutation | Killing test |
|---|---|---|
| `operation/wire_op.rs:176-177` stamp of `taper_angle` | both `h.write` lines dropped | `wire_taper_angle::the_corner_rule_and_the_dialect_each_move_the_stamp` (mitre != cone, U/V != mitre, U/V != cone) |
| `wire-iso.cps:205` `angle4` | refuse line deleted | `script_wire_iso::an_angle_word_section_posts_and_each_missing_piece_is_refused_by_name` (zero taper; WireFourAxis) |
| `wire-iso.cps:210` `acode` | refuse line deleted | same test (no `edm.codes.taper_angle`) |
| `wire-iso.cps:216` `angtpl` | refuse line deleted | same test (template without `{angle}`) |
| `wire-iso.cps:305` `ang` | refuse line deleted | same test (`WireAngle` with no dialect) |
| `posting_wire.rs:166` 4-axis refusal (now in `angle_lean`) | `if false && four` | `posting::wire::tests::an_angle_lean_refuses_a_four_axis_cut_an_unstated_rule_and_an_unresolved_top` |
| `posting_wire.rs:170` `complete()` | rules defaulted | same test |
| `posting_wire.rs:171` top unresolved | `top.unwrap_or(0.0)` | same test |
| `posting_wire.rs:326` lean changes side | `return Err` deleted | `posting::wire::tests::a_lean_that_changes_side_or_never_leans_is_refused_by_name` |
| `posting_wire.rs:333` no leaning side | `sign.unwrap_or(1.0)` | same test |
| `edm_taper.rs:89` not an object | `if false && !v.is_object()` | `machine::edm_taper::tests::a_taper_angle_not_an_object_or_a_garbled_side_refuses_the_file` |
| `edm_taper.rs:103` `positive` garble | `.unwrap_or(AngleSide::TopLeft)` | same test |
| `edm.rs:81` `"taper_angle"` in `WIRE_KEYS` | key dropped (array of 5) | `machine::edm::tests::a_sinker_stating_taper_angle_is_refused_as_a_wire_key` |
| `motion/src/wire_edm/taper.rs:222` cone turn-back | `if false && phi.abs() > ...` | `wire_edm::taper::tests::the_cone_rule_refuses_a_ring_that_turns_back_on_itself` |

Why 166/170/171 are pinned and not removed: generation's door (`wire_op::corner_rule`) and the stamp keep these cases out of a real post today. They stay as the post's own guard, so a 4-axis path never posts with angle words if it reaches the post some other way. `angle_lean` makes that guard testable.
